atomicity_checks.evidence: The authorized Eval Dataset version and a tenant-scoped canonical manifest hash over Dataset metadata and sorted examples are bound into runtime, release, and evaluation identities. Content mutation makes completion and publication fail closed.

Actor iteration 4 locks the Eval Dataset parent FOR UPDATE and every manifest example FOR SHARE inside promotion. Real two-connection PostgreSQL cases prove both an existing-example update and a new-example insert remain blocked after manifest resolution until the publication transaction commits; neither can make accepted Eval evidence stale inside the atomic decision window.
PostgreSQL persists queued, running, and terminal events; only valid transitions are allowed, cancellation can win the completion race, and every terminal row is immutable.

A tenant-operation-key advisory transaction lock serializes different Agents before release writes. A two-connection PostgreSQL race produces one result and one stable AGENT_RELEASE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, with no raw 23505 or duplicate Version, pointer, event, or request.
List/detail recompute the current server candidate and expose explicit Draft, model, resource, Dataset, runtime, release, and evaluation identity stale reasons without mutating stored evidence.

Actor iteration 3 requires the database-backed path to invoke the supplied current-readiness revalidator while model/provider rows remain locked. Missing proof fails unverifiable; revoked readiness invokes the callback once and leaves publish Version/Publication/event/request counts at 0/0/0/0, while rollback preserves its pointer and every release-row count.
A changed Draft revision/spec or current runtime identity rejects prior evidence before Version, Publication, event, or release-request creation.
The same tenant/operation/key/request returns the original Version, Publication, and event after mutable state changes; a different request hash returns AGENT_RELEASE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
Forced publish-event failure rolls back Version materialization, normalized bindings, Publication pointer, event, and idempotency request together.
PostgreSQL rejects invalid lifecycle transitions plus UPDATE or DELETE of terminal evaluations, evaluation events, Versions, publish events, and completed release requests.
Revoked, unavailable, current, foreign, and never-targeted rollback Versions leave the Publication pointer, audit-event count, and release-request count unchanged.
Credential-, token-, password-, bearer-, connection-, and key-shaped publish or rollback reasons are rejected before immutable audit persistence.

live_stack.provider_free_evidence: Against the real Gateway/PostgreSQL stack, one stable Eval Dataset and example produced a content hash, queued-to-cancelled evidence, queued-to-running-to-passed evidence, two immutable Versions, two promotions, and one audited rollback.
live_stack.provider_boundary: After restoring stub=false, the same live browser flow returned AGENT_RUNTIME_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE before an evaluation row and observed zero Version, Publication pointer, and publish event. No provider credential was read, changed, printed, or called.

non_passing_attempts: The first focused C-06 invocation failed 2/2 because the PostgreSQL test helper had not supplied the now-required readiness proof; the helper was corrected and the focused rerun passed 2/2.

The first iteration-3 live provider-free browser attempt failed before Agent work because VITE_API_URL caused a cross-origin direct request and the app cleared auth after the network failure; same-origin VITE_API_BASE_URL=/ fixed the harness and the final live run passed 1/1.

The first iteration-4 isolation attempt ran against freshly recreated release-image code and failed 2/6 because that image did not activate the current source stub path; after hot-syncing current source into the same provider-blank containers, the required rerun passed 6/6 with zero skips.
